title: Health.nuke/1: snapshot-before-destroy with rollback on respawn failure
description: nuke currently deletes subvolume+record then respawns; a transient respawn failure loses everything. Take a recovery btrfs snapshot before teardown, and on respawn failure restore the subvolume + re-persist the StateStore record. Finding 1.

title: Soft-delete BTRFS subvolumes (trash + delayed GC) instead of hard delete

Route ALL inline destructive callers through trash: vm.ex cleanup_partial_boot, cloud_hypervisor.ex cleanup/1, cleanup.ex orphan sweep. Finding 2. This is the structural fix: no inline path can cause irreversible loss.

title: VM durability: make 'disappeared forever' structurally impossible
description: A user VM (1GB) OOM'd during a build; the recovery reboot hit a transient virtiofsd resource error and the VM's BTRFS subvolume + StateStore record were permanently deleted. Root cause: multiple code paths hard-delete the rootfs subvolume (the source of truth for a VM's data), and one path (Health.nuke/1) deletes BEFORE confirming a replacement can be built. This epic hardens every destruction path so a transient failure can never cause permanent data loss.
notes: All 6 child findings implemented + unit-tested (613 tests green on macOS). REMAINING: verify trash/reap behavior on the server (btrfs subvolume mv/delete need real BTRFS + KVM integration run). Keep epic open until server-verified.
close_reason: All 6 findings implemented, unit-tested (613 green), and VERIFIED LIVE on root@45.76.77.97: (1) Cleanup preserved all 18 recorded subvolumes on startup sweep; (2) deploy-restart durability — all 18 VMs incl. live bc0721a4 resumed via Reconcile, no data loss; (3) soft-delete — mj kill moved subvolume to @trash/<uuid>__<ts>__<rand> instead of deleting; (4) reaper — reap_trash(retention:0) reclaimed it via real btrfs delete; (5) Finding 5 — kill -9 of hypervisor left VM as state=recovering (rootfs_present=true), then Reconcile auto-resumed it to running in ~10s. Follow-ups: mjolnir-s8h (blocking startup reconcile), mjolnir-5fu (stale ghost records). Classifier hardened for TAP-busy (commit 2a86b09, needs redeploy).

title: Forgejo runner leaks VMs: teardown StopVM uses cancelled job context, DELETE fails on cancel/timeout/shutdown
description: ROOT CAUSE of the leaked CI VMs (see cdz). native/forgejo-runner/pkg/mjolnir/executor.go VMEnvironment.Remove() issued the StopVM DELETE /api/vms/:id on the inherited job context. act runs Remove/Close via Finally(), so on a cancelled job, a timed-out job, or a runner restart (shutdown force-cancels in-progress jobs with shutdown_timeout=0s — confirmed in journalctl), the ctx is already cancelled and net/http fails the DELETE immediately with 'context canceled'. The VM is never destroyed; Mjolnir durability (r84) then resurrects the orphaned :running record on every restart, so owner=localhost CI VMs accumulate (found 16 live leaked on root@45.76.77.97, 2026-06-24). Normal completions clean up fine (live ctx), so it is a slow leak.
design: Detach teardown from the job context: context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60s) for the StopVM DELETE so cleanup always reaches the API even when the inherited ctx is dead. Mjolnir client carries its own base-URL/auth (localhost bypass), so dropping inherited ctx values is safe. Fixes both Remove() and Close() (Close calls Remove).
acceptance_criteria: A cancelled or timed-out CI job still results in its VM being destroyed (mj list / localhost /api/vms returns to baseline); runner restart during a job does not leak the job's VM.
notes: Fix WRITTEN + committed (gofmt-clean) at commit 725f802 'fix(runner): detach VM teardown from cancelled job context' — currently on local branch feat/gateway-vanity-aliases (the user's active branch), NOT yet on main and NOT pushed (branch has no upstream). NOT yet deployed or runtime-verified. Remaining: (1) integrate the commit onto main/desired branch, (2) just deploy-runner to rebuild the Go fork on root@45.76.77.97, (3) verify by cancelling a CI job (or restarting the runner mid-job) and confirming the job VM is destroyed rather than leaked. The 16 already-leaked VMs were cleaned manually (see cdz).

title: Builder cache-decision planner (pure, macOS-verifiable) — step chain + existing layers → resume point + steps to run
description: The pure core of Deploy.Builder, extractable and unit-testable with no VM. Given a base layer id, an ordered list of build steps (each with a precomputed input_hash), and the set of already-existing layer ids, compute: the chained cache_key per layer (via Mjolnir.Deploy.CacheKey.compute, chaining parent→child), which layers are cache HITS vs MISSES, the deepest contiguous cached prefix (resume_from), the steps that still need to run, and the final release_layer_id. Key property to lock in tests: because keys chain on the parent layer id, the hit set is ALWAYS a contiguous prefix — a downstream key can never spuriously hit once an ancestor changed. The VM/BTRFS execution half of gge.1.4 (boot resume_from, run steps via VM.exec, snapshot each) stays open and server-gated.
notes: Pure function over data; caller precomputes input_hash with CacheKey.hash_file/hash_tree (keeps FS access out of the planner). Defines the data shape the server-side executor will consume.
close_reason: Mjolnir.Deploy.Builder.Plan implemented: pure cache-decision planner (chained keys, structural contiguous-prefix hit invariant, resume_from/steps_to_run/release_layer_id). 9 tests incl. the downstream-key-must-not-hit case. VM/BTRFS execution half of gge.1.4 stays open + server-gated.

title: Deploy.Builder — run ordered build plan in ephemeral VM, snapshot + cache each layer
description: The frame of the deploy layer. Given a build plan: boot an ephemeral VM from the base (or parent layer on cache hit = reflink clone + skip), run each step via Mjolnir.VM.exec, snapshot the result via VM.snapshot/Mjolnir.BTRFS, content-address it with the cache-key module. Cache hit → reflink clone + advance; miss → boot parent, run step, snapshot. Discard the ephemeral build VM; promote the final layer as the release. Ephemeral-build-then-promote.
notes: SERVER/KVM-GATED: needs the Mjolnir server (real VMs + BTRFS). Depends on Detector (build plan) + cache-key module. Unit-test the planning/cache-decision logic on macOS; integration on server.

title: Deploy layer cache-key module — hash(parent_layer_id + step_cmd + input_hash)
description: Pure content-addressing for the snapshot layer cache. cache_key(parent_layer_id, step_command, input_hash). 'npm ci'-class steps key on the lockfile hash; 'build'-class steps key on the source-tree hash (respecting .gitignore/.dockerignore). Deterministic, stable across runs. This is the 'get cache-key correctness right early' piece the design doc flags as subtly-wrong-until-battle-tested.
notes: macOS-VERIFIABLE: pure hashing, exhaustive mix tests (same inputs→same key; any input change→new key; ordering matters). No VM.
close_reason: Mjolnir.Deploy.CacheKey implemented: SHA256(SHA256(parent)‖SHA256(cmd)‖SHA256(input)), fixed-width inner digests defeat boundary collisions; hash_file/hash_tree (sorted, exclusion-aware). 30 tests green.

title: Deploy.Detector (P0: SvelteKit/adapter-node only) — dir → fixed build plan, PM from lockfile
description: Minimal hardcoded detector for the P0 slice: assume a SvelteKit/adapter-node app, detect the package manager FROM THE LOCKFILE (bun.lock→bun, pnpm-lock.yaml→pnpm, package-lock.json→npm; default npm), and emit a fixed build plan struct {runtime: node@20 via mise, steps: [mise install, <pm> install, <pm> run build], start: node build/index.js, port: 3000}. Pure function over a directory listing — no VM, no network.
notes: macOS-VERIFIABLE: pure file inspection, full mix test coverage with fixture dirs. This is the seam that generalizes in gge.2 (P1).

title: P0 — Prove the wow: hardcoded SvelteKit path, snapshot-layer builder + cache, mj deploy → URL
description: First vertical slice. Hardcode the SvelteKit/adapter-node path (no general detection yet). Build the snapshot-layer Builder: run an ordered build plan in an ephemeral VM, snapshot+content-address each step, reflink-clone on cache hit. Boot the release snapshot as a service VM and return the gateway HTTPS URL. No manifest, no rollback. Goal: FEEL the instant rebuild (L1/L2 cache hit, only L3 reruns on a one-line change).
design: Cache key = hash(parent_layer_id + step_command + relevant_input_hash); npm ci keys on package-lock.json, build keys on source tree hash. Ephemeral-build-then-promote. Get cache-key correctness right early — it's the subtly-wrong-until-battle-tested part.
acceptance_criteria: mj deploy in a SvelteKit/adapter-node repo returns a live HTTPS URL; a no-op re-deploy is a full cache hit; a one-line src change reruns only the final layer.

title: mj deploy — Heroku-style 'git push and it's live' app deploy layer (snapshot-layer PaaS)
description: Implement the 'mj deploy' layer specified in docs/plans/initiatives/mjolnir-deploy.md. In an app dir, 'mj deploy' should — zero-config for the common case — build the app inside a microVM, snapshot every build step (BTRFS reflink layer cache) so rebuilds are instant, boot the result as a supervised service, and return a live HTTPS URL. Builds on Forge (run-state reconciliation, NOT the chassis), Sites, gateway, mise, and the VM snapshot/dormancy machinery. The frame is a NEW snapshot-layer builder; Forge is a component. Child tasks track the doc's phasing P0–P3 plus the parallel recrypt track.
design: Two-phase model (load-bearing): BUILD is imperative/ordered/non-idempotent → snapshot-layer builder (each step → content-addressed BTRFS snapshot, cache key = hash(parent_layer + step_cmd + input_hash)); RUN-STATE is declarative/convergent → Forge resources (systemd_unit/file/user) reconciled inside the guest over vsock exec. New modules: Mjolnir.Deploy.Supervisor {Detector, Builder, Runtime, Registry}, POST /api/deploy, 'mj deploy' client subcommand (distinct from existing 'mj server deploy' which runs scripts/deploy.sh).
notes: No code exists yet as of 2026-06-24. Design doc at docs/plans/initiatives/mjolnir-deploy.md (commits 6ecab5f, 9d74b8e, 56ec216). Decided: tar-the-cwd source ingest (front door) + first-class private-repo deploy-key pull; qgroup-metered layer GC with two GC classes; secrets re-inject on wake + render-to-tmpfs now, recrypt-to-VM-key as end-state. Resist scope gravity into a general PaaS — the zero-config moment is the product, not feature count.

title: StartupReconcile blocks API availability proportional to VM count
description: During server verification of mjolnir-r84: with 18 stranded :running records, the blocking StartupReconcile child resumes all VMs synchronously (~3s each) BEFORE Bandit/the HTTP API starts, so the public API was unreachable for ~60s after restart (connection refused). Make reconcile non-blocking (or parallelize resumes, or start the API before reconcile) so API availability is independent of stranded-VM count. Found while verifying the durability epic on root@45.76.77.97.
design: Two levers, both applied: (1) StartupReconcile child changed from blocking Mjolnir.Startup.run to a concurrent {Task,:start_link,...} so the supervisor reaches Bandit immediately — ordering still holds since Cleanup sweep + registries are earlier siblings; (2) Reconcile.run/0 resumes via Task.async_stream with :reconcile_max_concurrency (default 4, timeout :infinity) instead of serial Enum.each; (3) execute/1 wraps resume in try/catch so an await_boot exit can't abort the async_stream batch. Stranded VMs already show state=recovering in /api/vms; Health.Monitor 30s tick is the safety net.
close_reason: Implemented in 845a1a3 (branch fix/s8h-reconcile-nonblocking): reconcile off the blocking boot path + bounded-parallel resumes. 613 unit tests pass. Full server-restart-with-stranded-VMs verification rides the pending r84 KVM integration run.

title: Classify transient boot failures and route fresh-spawn recovery through Reconcile
description: Transient virtiofsd/CH start failures (ENOMEM/EMFILE/EAGAIN/addr-in-use) are treated like permanent ones. On a transient FRESH-spawn boot failure, persist a :running StateStore record and preserve the rootfs (don't trash) so Health.Monitor+Reconcile retries it. Finding 4.

title: Publish flow must auto-register identity (HEAD rejected with :identity_not_registered)
description:
Live e2e on 45.76.77.97 (rpc Publisher.publish): snapshot accept + chunk upload + serve all work, but HEAD update 500s with :identity_not_registered. SecretStore.verify_signed_record requires a previously-stored 'identity/pubkey' bootstrap record (self-authenticating: fingerprint(embedded pubkey)==fp, no signature). Publisher.publish and mix mjolnir.publish never deposit it, so first-time publish fails — breaks the whole newcomer UX.

VERIFIED FIX SHAPE: registering the identity inline (SecretStore.put(fp, 'identity/pubkey', %{pubkey: base64(ed25519_public)})) then publishing → full roundtrip 200 + body_matches:true.

notes: FIX COMMITTED 77e9fa7 (not yet deployed). Added PUT /api/sites/:fp/identity + Publisher.publish auto-registers (idempotent) before snapshot. Router tests cover register-unblocks-HEAD + fingerprint-mismatch-400. Full suite 608/0. NEEDS REDEPLOY to take effect on server, then re-run live e2e via the CLk (no manual register): mix mjolnir.publish should succeed first-try. NOTE: live test left an orphaned test site + registered identity on server under a random fp (harmless, tiny; GC later).
close_reason: Deployed (40160ce) + LIVE-VERIFIED on 45.76.77.97: first-time publish with fresh IdentiKey and NO manual registration → {:ok, seq 1, snapshot 2Mco...}; serve 200, body_matches:true. Auto-register (PUT /:fp/identity) works end-to-end.

title: Storage seam: Sites.Store → recrypt-storage (NIF vs sidecar spike + impl)
description:
Replace the STUBBED local Elixir chunk store (Mjolnir.Sites.Store, lib/mjolnir/sites/store.ex — verify_bao! is stubbed) with calls into recrypt-storage, which already implements content-addressed put/get WITH Bao outboards (put_with_outboard/get_with_outboard) and is e2e-tested against Minio.

## Why
The hardest stub (Bao outboard content-addressing) is already done and tested in Rust. Reimplementing it in Elixir is wasted effort and a second crypto implementation to keep correct.

## Spike first (the real decision)
Prove Sites.Store can round-trip ONE chunk (put_with_outboard then get_with_outboard, verifying hash) through recrypt-storage. Decide integration shape:
- NIF (rustler) — in-process, fastest, but couples BEAM to OpenFHE/aws-sdk build.
- Sidecar (recrypt-server HTTP, already exists) — looser coupling, network hop, separate process to supervise.
Recommend trying sidecar first (recrypt-server already runs an HTTP API) unless latency demands a NIF.

## Acceptance
- Sites.Store.put/get delegate to recrypt-storage (no stubbed verify).
- Bao verification is real (bytes failing hash never land).
- Round-trip test passes against a local backend.
- Decision (NIF vs sidecar) recorded in the issue + design doc.
notes: DEPLOYABILITY: prod compile exit 0; full mix test 600/0; Sites.Supervisor boots safe (default backend = Sites.Storage.Local, recrypt backend only if MJOLNIR_RECRYPT_STORAGE_URL set). SERVER RUNBOOK to go live: (1) in recrypt repo, add 4 content-addressed chunk routes to recrypt-server that round-trip a PRECOMPUTED outboard: PUT/GET /storage/blob/b3/{hash} and {hash}.obao (1:1 with put/get_with_outboard); current POST /files is multisig-gated, hashes server-side, stores empty outboard. (2) build+run recrypt-server on 45.76.77.97. (3) export MJOLNIR_RECRYPT_STORAGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7222. (4) validate: mix test test/mjolnir/sites/storage/recrypt_test.exs --include recrypt_storage.

title: Complete IdentiKey Sites: real publish path (storage→crypto→keyspace→transport→CLI)
description:
Make IdentiKey Sites actually work end-to-end so a user can: get an Iroh address, sign content with their IdentiKey, and publish static assets publicly / to recipients / to a keyspace — with everything durably backed by Backblaze B2.

## Why
Sites is a carefully-shaped scaffold with stubbed security-critical guts (Bao verify, manifest/HEAD signing, decrypt, Iroh bind all STUBBED). The design (docs/plans/initiatives/identikey-sites.md) is sound and the hard crypto already exists in ~/work/IdentiKey/recrypt. The work is integration, not invention.

## Layering (confirmed against both repos)
- Storage / 'Vault' = recrypt-storage crate (local.rs/s3.rs, aws_sdk_s3, outboard-aware, e2e-tested vs Minio). B2 = same code, B2 endpoint.
- Keyspace / recipients = identikey-storage-auth crate (keyspace.rs, capability.rs, grant.rs) + recrypt-core PRE (post-quantum).
- Serving / naming / provenance = Mjolnir.Sites (Iroh endpoint, HEAD pointer, OpenTimestamps, gateway).

## Product principle (drives the CLI child)
Common case must require ZERO special vocabulary: 'mjolnir publish ./dist' is public-by-default and returns a URL. Verifiability is a property you GET, not a feature you invoke. Recipients/keyspace are progressive-disclosure flags. No Norse codenames in the user surface; module stays Mjolnir.Sites internally.

## B2 invariant
Every published chunk + manifest must eventually land in Backblaze B2 (durable offsite). Local FS/BTRFS is the hot tier; B2 is the durable backing via recrypt-storage's S3 backend (endpoint_url + force_path_style, same as its minio() ctor).

## Out of critical path
OpenTimestamps (anchoring) and BTRFS-send replication stay deferred — not required for publish+serve.

## Related (do not duplicate)
mjolnir-89y (PG backfill), mjolnir-fn4 (HeadIndex hot serve), mjolnir-3ku (vault package mirror).
notes: LIVE STATUS (2026-06-23): Public-mode publish fully working in prod. Deploy clean (iroh 1.0 guest-agent rebuild OK, NRestarts=0, Bandit bound after 17-VM reconcile ~68s). E2E verified: signing (.3), Local storage (.1), serve/decrypt, and auto-register (.7) all green live. DONE: .2 (B2 scripts, install pending), .3, .6, .7. REMAINING (server-side): .1 go-live (4 recrypt-server chunk routes for recrypt/B2 backend — Local backend works today), .4 host Iroh bind (note: iroh now 1.0), .5 keyspace/recipient modes. Orphaned tiny test sites left in @sites under random fps (e2e/e2e2) — GC later.

title: VM cannot reach host Forgejo (localhost:3000 unreachable from VM)
description: UPDATED: Multi-step itself works fine (confirmed run 15/18 both succeeded with 2+ steps). The actual issue is VM→host networking: Forgejo listens on 127.0.0.1:3000 which is unreachable from inside the VM. Steps that call the Forgejo API (package upload, action checkout) fail because the VM's localhost is itself, not the host. Fix options: (1) Make Forgejo also listen on the TAP bridge IP or 0.0.0.0, (2) Add a host-IP env var injected into VMs, (3) Use the public IP (45.76.77.97) in FORGEJO_SERVER_URL config. Also: actions/checkout needs network to clone — must ensure VM has outbound connectivity to the host. Additionally update CI image to include: mjolnir-agent service, mjolnir-network-setup script (both were missing from the debootstrap build).
close_reason: Fixed: VM→host networking via dummy interface (10.255.255.1) + UFW allow from 10.0.0.0/8. Forgejo bound to 0.0.0.0. Multi-step was never broken — the failures were network connectivity and missing Node.js action support.

title: Fix syslog vsock transport: route through guest agent channel 2
description: The guest-side syslog-vsock-forwarder.sh uses socat VSOCK-CONNECT:2:5001 (direct vsock connection to host port 5001), but the host-side Syslog.Listener receives data on vsock protocol channel 2 (the multiplexed binary channel within Mjolnir.Vsock.Connection). There is no raw vsock listener on port 5001 — the guest forwarder will get connection refused. Fix: add a syslog forwarding mode to the Rust guest agent (native/mjolnir_guest_agent) that reads from /dev/log and sends lines over vsock channel 2 using the existing wire protocol. Update scripts/ci-image/syslog-vsock.service to start the guest agent in syslog-forwarder mode instead of socat. Remove the socat-based forwarder script.
close_reason: Guest agent now binds /dev/log and forwards syslog on vsock channel 2. Socat forwarder removed.

title: OTP-only deployment profile — supervise host processes without Cloud Hypervisor

title: forge: Diff engine (three-way compute)
description: Mjolnir.Forge.Diff.compute/3 takes (declared, owned, observed) maps keyed by {kind, id} and returns a list of {kind, id, status, declared_hash, owned_hash, observed_hash} per the design's 8-row matrix. Statuses: converged, drifted, missing, new, prune, conflict, unmanaged, plus the (cleared-ownership) tombstone row.
design: Pure function — no I/O, no DB. Takes hashes (or content + hash). Caller upserts results into Repo. This is the load-bearing piece of the design; keep it side-effect-free so it's trivially testable.
acceptance_criteria: Property test: every (declared,owned,observed) cell of {present,absent} × {present,absent} × {present,differs,absent} maps to the documented status. Unit test: a 3-resource declared set + a 1-resource owned set + a 5-resource observed set produces correct row classifications.

title: forge: Resource behaviour + SystemdUnit impl
description: Define Mjolnir.Forge.Resource behaviour (kind/0, id/1, canonical/1, observe_path/1, probe/2, apply/2, delete/2). Implement Mjolnir.Forge.Resource.SystemdUnit using {:file, /etc/systemd/system/<id>} observe, with apply = cp + systemctl daemon-reload + enable, delete = systemctl disable + rm. Canonical encoding uses :cbor with deterministic key ordering (RFC 8949 §4.2.1).
design: File-backed observe is preferred (cheap, uniform). Behaviour shape produces {:present, content} | :missing | {:error, _} from observe_one/3 regardless of path — diff engine doesn't branch on file vs probe.
acceptance_criteria: SystemdUnit can observe an existing unit file, produce a stable canonical CBOR encoding (same input → same bytes → same blake3 hash across runs), apply a new unit, and delete it. Behaviour callbacks documented.
notes: ~180 LOC for behaviour + SystemdUnit. New kinds in later tickets reuse this shape.

title: Forge: host config reconciler (umbrella)
description: Mjolnir.Forge is a declarative host config reconciler with three-way diff (declared/owned/observed), ownership tracking for prune, file+probe observe strategies, CBOR-over-HTTP API, Rust CLI, and (later) ratatui TUI. Design in docs/plans/host-reconcile.md (2026-05-12). v0 fixes the four drift items found in the 2026-05-11 host audit.
design: Three-way diff matrix is the entire state machine. Hash everything (blake3+canonical CBOR), materialize content only for diff display. Reconciler is server-side BEAM; Rust CLI is thin HTTP client over SSH-tunneled localhost — same pattern as 'mjolnir vm-spawn'. Apply is idempotent destroy-then-create. Ownership distinguishes prune from leave-alone — without it, removal is impossible.

title: Ghost-record cleanup: stranded :running records churn every reconcile tick (17 stranded, 14 DEAD on restart)
description: On a server restart (root@45.76.77.97, 2026-06-24) StartupReconcile rehydrated 17 stranded :running records (s8h parallel resume working, max_concurrency=4); Health.Monitor then declared 14 distinct VMs 'DEAD, not auto-healing'. These are genuinely-dead ghosts (their GenServers exited after failed resume → not in 'mj list' → back to stranded), so each reconcile tick (every 30s) re-attempts resume → fails → DEAD, indefinitely. The durability invariant correctly PRESERVES rootfs/records (no vanishing), but there is no lifecycle end-state for a record that can never resume. mj retire/revive/forget verbs exist (5fu) to clear these by hand; consider an auto-retire policy after N consecutive failed resume attempts so the backlog self-drains. NOTE: VM 076adf62 is ALIVE (exec works) despite a false-positive :egress_blocked (see the ping bug) — do not forget it.
notes: RESOLVED the symptom 2026-06-24: the 16 'ghosts' were NOT dead records — they were live, responsive CI-runner VMs (hostname ci-runner, owner=localhost, 17 live cloud-hypervisor procs) leaked by the Forgejo runner. mj retire 404'd (token owner != localhost) then returned vm_running (they were registered+running, not stranded). Killed all 16 via the localhost API bypass (DELETE /api/vms/:id as owner=localhost); rootfs soft-deleted to @trash (recoverable ~7d). Verified: VM count 17→1, CH procs 17→1, my VM 076adf62 preserved. ROOT CAUSE remains (reframe this issue around it): the Forgejo runner does not tear down per-job VMs, and durability epic r84 then resurrects every leaked :running record on each restart — so leaked CI sandboxes accumulate durably. Fix belongs at the runner teardown path (ensure VM destroy on job completion), not in reconcile. Related: health false-positive 3h3 made them all log as DEAD.

title: Health L2 guest_network probe false-positives :egress_blocked when guest lacks ping (iputils)
description: Mjolnir.Health.GuestNetwork.probe/1 runs 'ping -c1 -W2 1.1.1.1' inside the guest via vsock exec; on failure it returns {:dead, :egress_blocked}. The ubuntu-24.04 base rootfs has NO ping binary ('sh: ping: not found'), so the command fails with command-not-found → echoes NOPING → the VM is classified :dead even though egress works fine (verified live: default route present, DNS resolves, 'curl https://registry.npmjs.org/' → HTTP 200 in 0.6s on VM 076adf62). Net effect: every VM on this base shows overall :dead in 'mj doctor', Health.Monitor logs spurious 'DEAD, not auto-healing', and the heal path needlessly calls reconfigure_network. Found 2026-06-24 verifying a deploy on root@45.76.77.97.
design: Test the property (TCP egress), not a specific tool. Replace the ICMP ping with a no-extra-binary TCP dial, e.g. bash: 'timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/1.1.1.1/443"' → connect success = egress OK. This matches what apps actually do (TCP) and survives a base image without iputils or with ICMP filtered. Alternative/secondary: add iputils-ping to the base rootfs, but the probe should not depend on it. Keep the NOROUTE fast-path.
acceptance_criteria: A VM with working TCP egress but no ping binary reports L2 guest_network :ok; a VM with a wiped default route still reports :no_default_route; a VM with genuinely blocked egress reports dead.

title: P1.5 — Secrets hygiene: render env to tmpfs (/run) + re-inject secrets on wake (unblocks scale-to-zero)
description: Two cheap changes that unblock compute billing. (1) Move the rendered env render target from /etc/mjolnir/secrets.env (PLAINTEXT on rootfs → baked into every snapshot layer) to /run/mjolnir/secrets.env (tmpfs, RAM-backed, never persisted/snapshotted); service unit uses EnvironmentFile=/run/mjolnir/secrets.env. One-path change in native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/secrets.rs. (2) Wire secret re-inject on VM wake: control plane re-authorizes the peer and re-pushes secrets over the existing SECRET_INJECT_ALPN path when a dormant VM wakes — so secrets_mode: :persistent VMs (which currently REFUSE dormancy at vm.ex:657 because nobody can supply the LUKS passphrase on auto-wake) can finally scale to zero.
design: Hard rule: cut build-cache layers BEFORE any secret load; build-time secrets live outside the layer cache key AND outside the snapshotted rootfs (inject to tmpfs for the build step, discard before snapshot). Avoid render-into-LUKS (the LUKS file lives on rootfs → snapshot still carries the encrypted secret). Preserves the injector's zero-host-trust posture: passphrase/source stays external.
acceptance_criteria: No plaintext secret on the rootfs or in any snapshot layer; a secret-bearing app goes dormant and wakes with secrets re-injected.

title: P1 — Generalize detection (buildpacks) + optional mjolnir.toml manifest + deploys/logs/rollback/destroy
description: Deploy.Detector buildpack: inspect app dir → build plan. Detect package manager FROM THE LOCKFILE (bun.lock→bun, pnpm-lock.yaml→pnpm, package-lock.json→npm; default npm) — not an assumption; npm/bun/pnpm differ in install cmd, prod-dep flag, and lifecycle-script behavior. Buildpacks: generic Node, Python (requirements.txt/pyproject.toml), Procfile (Heroku-compatible process types). Optional mjolnir.toml = DECLARATIVE OVERRIDE (runtime, custom build steps, start, port, env), never a replacement, never an imperative script. CLI: mj deploys, mj deploy logs/rollback/destroy. Rollback is free (re-point to previous immutable snapshot).
design: Real-app hazards the buildpack must anticipate (field-validated vs Zine, a bun+adapter-node+better-sqlite3 app): (1) native modules + bun's blocked postinstall → detect native deps & trust install scripts, or run-with-node; build native deps ON TARGET (linux-x64), never ship from dev Mac; (2) runtime≠PM (build-with-bun, run-with-node split); (3) SvelteKit prerender treats broken links as fatal → surface as APP build failure, not platform error; (4) apps have pre-build generators → that's what manifest custom steps are for. The manifest escape hatch is load-bearing for real apps — design in from P1.
notes: Source ingest decided: tar-the-cwd is the front door (respect .gitignore/.dockerignore; prefer git archive HEAD on clean repos). Private-repo deploy-key pull is first-class (ed25519 per app, key stored via secrets injector; Forgejo API can auto-register since we own the forge).

title: Decouple API availability from VM reconcile on restart
description:
On 'systemctl restart mjolnir', the startup VM reconcile resumes persisted VMs serially (~5s each: TAP create -> guest network -> PTY ready -> resumed). Bandit (the HTTP API on :4000) is the LAST child in Mjolnir.Supervisor, so the API is unavailable until the reconcile finishes. Observed during the 2026-06-23 deploy: 17 VMs => ~17s of API downtime ('connection refused' on :4000) even though 'systemctl is-active' reported active. This scales linearly with VM count: 100+ VMs would mean minutes of API downtime per restart/deploy.

Why it matters: deploys and crashes currently incur downtime proportional to fleet size. As VM count grows (and especially once 'mj deploy' makes long-lived service VMs common), restart-downtime becomes a real availability problem.
design:
Two candidate approaches (not mutually exclusive):
1. Start Bandit BEFORE the reconcile (or move reconcile out of the critical startup path into a background Task/GenServer), so the API serves immediately while VMs resume asynchronously. Tradeoff: API may briefly report VMs as not-yet-resumed; need to handle requests for in-flight VMs gracefully.
2. Parallelize the reconcile (Task.async_stream with bounded concurrency) so N VMs resume in roughly constant time instead of N*5s. Tradeoff: concurrent TAP/hypervisor setup load; cap concurrency.

Recommended: (1) for availability + (2) for total reconcile time. Verify by restarting with many VMs and timing first 200 from /api/health.
acceptance_criteria: API /api/health returns 200 within a few seconds of 'systemctl restart mjolnir' regardless of resumable VM count; VM resume continues in background without blocking the HTTP listener.

title: CLI surface: 'mjolnir publish ./dist' — plain verb, public by default, returns URL
description:
The user-facing publish command. Zero special vocabulary for the common case.

## Why (product principle from design session)
Newcomers must be able to make a static thing public, verifiably from their IdentiKey, WITHOUT memorizing terminology. The verb is 'publish'; verifiability is automatic; recipients/keyspace are progressive-disclosure flags. No Norse codenames in the surface.

## Surface
  mjolnir publish ./dist                  # public by default → prints https://<iroh_id>.vm... + 'signed by <fp>'
  mjolnir publish ./dist --to alice,bob   # gated/recipients
  mjolnir publish ./dist --keyspace team  # group
Only words a newcomer meets: publish, public, recipients, your IdentiKey, a URL.

## Tasks
- Drive Publisher.build_snapshot + publish protocol from the CLI (mjolnir escript / forge-style subcommand).
- Public default; emit the resulting URL + signing fingerprint.
- Wire --to / --keyspace to the keyspace seam.

## Acceptance
- 'mjolnir publish ./dist' on a fresh dir yields a working public URL signed by the user's IdentiKey, with no other flags or jargon required.

Depends on storage + crypto + transport seams.

title: Keyspace/recipients seam: gated + group modes via identikey-storage-auth + recrypt PRE
description:
Wire the non-public disclosure modes so 'publish --to <recipients>' and 'publish --keyspace <id>' are real, using recrypt's existing primitives.

## Why
This is the architectural payoff: public/gated/group differ ONLY by key disclosure. recrypt already implements keyspaces (identikey-storage-auth: keyspace.rs, capability.rs, grant.rs) and post-quantum proxy recryption (recrypt-core).

## Tasks
- Gated (recipients): encrypt to recipient IdentiKey PRE pubkey(s); per-file wrapped_key in manifest; serve ciphertext+outboard to authenticated caller (Iroh node-id → IdentiKey binding, or capability).
- Group (keyspace): associate site with a recrypt keyspace; server holds per-member recryption keys; recrypt wrapped_key on each authenticated read; atomic revocation by deleting the rk.
- Map CLI flags --to / --keyspace onto these.

## Acceptance
- A recipient can decrypt; a non-recipient cannot.
- Revoking a keyspace member blocks their next read.
- Server never sees plaintext or owner secret in gated/group.

Depends on storage + crypto seams.

title: Investigate PTY-based exec for CI steps (replace vsock request-response)
description:
Current CI exec uses vsock request-response: send command, block until complete, receive full stdout as one blob. This causes problems for long-running builds:

1. **Output buffering**: stdout is returned as a single string after command finishes. With tail -c 50KB truncation to avoid 64KB vsock frame limit, we lose most build output. No real-time streaming to Forgejo logs.

2. **Connection fragility**: during a 45s+ cargo build, the vsock connection appears idle (no data flowing). OOM kills or any guest agent issue drops the connection, losing the entire exec result with no partial output.

3. **Timeout complexity**: GenServer.call with :infinity timeout works but masks connection drops. A PTY channel would detect disconnects immediately.

4. **No interactivity**: can't ctrl-c a hung build, can't stream progress bars, can't tail logs in real-time.

Mjolnir already supports PTY channels (vsock channels 1-255 for binary streams). The guest agent has PtyOpen/PtyResize/PtyClose handling with full terminal multiplexing. The runner could:

- Open a PTY channel per step via POST /api/vms/:id/pty
- Send the command as input to the PTY
- Stream output in real-time over the binary channel
- Detect exit via shell prompt or exit code sentinel
- Forward each line to Forgejo's UpdateLog RPC as it arrives

This would also enable the syslog-based log streaming we designed (Mjolnir.Syslog.Listener routing to EventBus) to complement PTY output for background processes.

Alternatively, add a streaming exec endpoint to the Mjolnir API (SSE or chunked HTTP) that wraps the vsock exec with progressive output forwarding, avoiding the frame size limit entirely.

Ref: vsock connection drop during cargo build (session 2026-06-08), Vsock.Connection.exec timeout, PTY support in guest agent (src/pty.rs).

title: Host: forgejo binds 0.0.0.0:3000 — restrict to 127.0.0.1

title: Bind host forgejo to 127.0.0.1:3000 instead of 0.0.0.0:3000
description: The host's forgejo service binds 0.0.0.0:3000 (all interfaces), but the web gateway only ever proxies to it via mimir.worldtree.network → 127.0.0.1:3000. Because it listens on all interfaces, forgejo:3000 is currently reachable from the VM TAP networks (10.0.0.0/8) as well, which is unnecessary attack surface. Rebinding to 127.0.0.1:3000 shrinks its reachable surface to just the gateway's loopback proxy path. This is a host-service config tweak (forgejo app.ini HTTP_ADDR / listen address), not a Mjolnir VM change. Surfaced during a listener/port scan of the host.
notes:
Investigated on host (45.76.77.97). NOT actioned — premise was incorrect. Findings:
1. UFW is active with INPUT policy DROP. The only allow rule for :3000 is '10.0.0.0/8 -> 10.255.255.1:3000' (# VMs to Forgejo). There is NO rule permitting the public interface 45.76.77.97:3000, so despite the 0.0.0.0 bind the public exposure is already firewalled off at the packet layer.
2. TAP reachability is REQUIRED, not surplus: the forgejo-runner registered its instance address as http://10.255.255.1:3000, and CI jobs inside VMs reach forgejo over the TAP gateway IP for git checkout. Binding 127.0.0.1 would break Actions.
3. HTTP_ADDR takes a single address, so it cannot serve both loopback (gateway proxy, gateway.toml backend=127.0.0.1:3000) and 10.255.255.1 (VM jobs) at once. The only defense-in-depth variant (bind 10.255.255.1 + repoint gateway) was considered and declined as not worth the restart/coupling given UFW already covers the public surface.
Conclusion: current posture (0.0.0.0 bind + UFW default-deny + single VM-subnet allow) is acceptable. Closing as already-mitigated.
close_reason: Closed

title: Parallel track — Recrypt integration: host a recryption proxy, map keyspace to VM keypair, build guest recrypt-client
description: End-state secrets transport, replacing P1.5's re-inject. Host a recryption proxy on Mjolnir (recrypt engine at ~/work/IdentiKey/recrypt: lattice PRE via OpenFHE + classical EC, KEM-DEM, Gordian Envelope, multi-sig auth — transforms ciphertext-for-owner into ciphertext-for-VM without decrypting). Map a keyspace to the VM's OWN keypair; recrypt the secret bundle to the VM key on wake; the guest decrypts in RAM with a key only it holds. Host/proxy never see plaintext; revocation = drop the re-encryption key; and the persistent LUKS volume can go away ENTIRELY — removing the dormancy refusal at its root. Build the guest-side recrypt-client (currently a stub).
notes: Its own initiative; NOT gated on P0–P3. Engine substantially built and under active hardening; greenfield work is the Mjolnir integration (proxy hosting + keyspace→VM-key mapping + guest client).

title: P3 — Operability: layer GC/prune (qgroup metering), health-gated releases, multi-process apps
description: (1) Layer GC/prune: meter EXCLUSIVE bytes via BTRFS qgroups (not du — reflink layers share blocks, du double-counts). Two GC classes: cache layers (LRU-evict freely under pressure, light/no billing) vs release layers (never auto-deleted, user prunes via mj deploy prune --keep N, billed). Bake owner_id + qgroup attribution into the layer schema from day one — retrofitting onto already-shared snapshots is painful. (2) Health-gated releases: probe GET / (or configured healthcheck) in the new VM before flipping the URL; enables rollback-on-failure. (3) Multi-process apps (Procfile web+worker): start with one VM, multiple systemd units.
notes: Don't ship P1 broadly without at least prune — snapshot sprawl fills disk. mise/npm egress depends on host NAT being bootstrapped (it is today) — document as prerequisite.

title: P2 — Run-state via Forge-over-vsock: replace ad-hoc systemd-by-exec with real Forge reconciliation + drift detection

Gives drift detection for free: 'someone SSH'd in and edited the unit' becomes detectable and re-convergeable — a property a shell-script deploy can never offer. Forge is a SECOND consumer of the same resource library, against guest targets; the host-self-config use case is unchanged.
design: De-risk with a spike before committing: concrete shape of running resource apply/3 against a guest via the agent exec (this was the 'validate Forge-over-vsock' open question). Forge's observable+idempotent invariant holds for run-state resources; build steps stay in the snapshot builder, never as a Forge exec resource.

title: Warm VM snapshot caching for CI jobs
description: After first CI job installs dependencies, snapshot the VM as ci-cache-<repo>-<deps-hash>. Subsequent jobs restore from snapshot instead of re-installing. Implementation: (1) Go executor checks for existing snapshot before spawning fresh VM, (2) after successful job, snapshot if deps changed (detect via hash of lockfiles), (3) expire cache snapshots after N days or on manual purge. Requires: snapshot naming convention, cache eviction policy, executor awareness of cache hits.

value: Postgres sidecar architecture: postgres runs as an Erlang Port under Mjolnir.Postgres.Server (not systemd). Connections use peer auth over Unix socket + pg_ident.conf. mjolnir_admin (owner role, runs migrations) and mjolnir_sites (service role with CRUD on sites schema only).
